en: Śrīḥ!

The Jayantīkalpa, among all the fundamental works composed by the venerable Lord Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda. Salutations to Śrī Lakṣmī-Hayagrīva, who is the essence of Śrīmat Hanumān, Abhinava Mādhva, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and Vedavyāsa.
When the eighth day of the dark fortnight occurs at midnight under the asterism Rohiṇī, it is called Jayantī; it is the destroyer of all sins.
Since the unborn Lord Hari himself was born in that month of Niśītha,
therefore that day is remembered as exceedingly meritorious and a destroyer of sins.
Therefore, that [day] named Jayantī should always be observed as a fast by all, especially by the twice-born and particularly by those devoted to Him. || 3 ||
He who eats on that day out of delusion eats pus and blood;
therefore, one should observe a fast on that meritorious day, endowed with faith.
Having performed purification according to the rule, the wise man, free from sloth, should perform his bath at the time of dawn for the sake of yoga, in accordance with the prescribed ritual.
One should perform the daily rites while remembering the Lord who has gone [to the forest]:
"Salutations again and again to Śrī Govinda, the source of yoga, the Lord of yoga, the Master of yoga. (6)
Furthermore, at midday and again in the evening, being unwearied,
he should bathe with the previous mantra while recollecting Vāsudeva.
Then, with a well-composed mind, a person endowed with faith and devotion should perform the worship according to the rules, using the mantra beginning with "yajñāya."
There one should worship Kṛṣṇa, Balabhadra, Vasudeva, Devakī, Nandagopa, Yaśodā, and Subhadrā;
having offered the respectful water (arghya), they should be worshipped when the lunar disc has risen.
He was born for the sake of slaying Kaṃsa, for the removal of the earth's burden,
for the destruction of the Kauravas, and for the death of the Daityas.
O Hari, for the sake of the welfare of the Pāṇḍavas and for the establishment of Dharma,
please accept this arghya offered by me together with Devakī.
O Moon, born from the ocean of Śrī, arisen from the eye of Atri,
accept this arghya offered by me together with Rohiṇī.

Having offered the *arghya* with this mantra and having performed the ritual worship (*upasthāna*) of the Moon, the wise one [should offer it] to Śaśin, to the divine Candra, to the divine Soma, and to Indu. (13)
Salutations to the deer-marked one, to the lunar orb, to the lamp of the world, to the illuminator, whose mind is attached to Rohiṇī, the lord of the stars. || 14 ||
Having withdrawn all that [into himself], the celibate student who has conquered his senses should then go to sleep while reciting the mantra beginning with "viśvāya. (15)

Then, having performed his daily obligatory rites (*nityāhnika*), he should give wealth according to his ability with the mantra "To Sarva" (*sarvāya*). Thereafter, he should perform the breaking of the fast (*pāraṇa*) with the mantra "To Dharma" (*dharmāya*). Thus established in well-being, he is liberated from all sins. (16)
Thus ends the *Jayantīkalpa* composed by the venerable teacher Śrīmad Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpādācārya.
Thus ends the Jayantī-kalpa.
May this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
